A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same authors' investigation of TabPFN v2. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, randomized-token experiments, feature-extraction results, scalability experiments, and component analyses in Sections 4–7 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds attention analyses, unsupervised embedding comparisons, forest-extension results, and dataset meta-feature analysis.

M1.justification: v2 adds a forest extension using 32 trees trained on 60% subsamples. Its underlying tree partitions use a minimum split size of 10,000, replacing v1's depth-5/10 rule. The randomized-token adaptations of FT-T and MNCA disappear. Leave-one-fold-out extraction and the permuted decimal-encoding procedure remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The underlying benchmark datasets and application tasks are retained, including the 12 many-class datasets already evaluated in v1. v2 Appendix D adds an auxiliary dataset-level classification task: predicting Good versus Bad TabPFN performance from meta-features. Including existing many-class datasets in the main aggregate does not introduce new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds TabM to the main benchmark comparison, PFN-v2-DPT to the many-class comparison, and Dummy and Permute unsupervised embedding methods to the feature-extraction comparison. These additions provide substantive new controls across several existing experiments (Figures 1–2 and 5; Tables 7, 11, and 13).

E3.justification: The reported main evaluation changes from 261 to 273 datasets, specifying ECOC for many-class tasks. High-dimensional feature bagging changes from four subsets to ceil(d/500) subsets of 500 attributes. New protocols include a group-size-one checkpoint for attention analysis and prediction-budget matching for DPT. The standard data split and 100-trial baseline tuning remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's FT-T/MNCA randomized-token transfer experiment is removed. v2 adds layer-wise attribute projections, attention maps and initialization stability analysis, supervised-versus-unsupervised embedding comparisons, a matched-budget decimal-encoding control, and a meta-feature decision-tree analysis. The existing feature-engineering and ensemble-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports attention-pattern cosine similarities and variability across 10 runs in Section 5.2 and Figure 3. Existing benchmark reporting retains 15 random seeds, mean/standard-deviation results, and the Wilcoxon-Holm test at 0.05; no increase in those benchmark runs is established.

E6.justification: All 29 Vanilla embedding accuracies change; website_phishing falls from 88.93% to 36.90% in v1 Table 10 versus v2 Table 13, while retained layer/combined accuracies stay unchanged. Under revised feature bagging, mean accuracy changes from 88.95% to 89.73%. DPT, forest, attention, and meta-feature results are added. PAMA changes from 25.06% to 26.02% under a different dataset pool and comparator set, so this is not a same-setting gain.

T1.justification: The tokenization formula changes non-equivalently from x_i^j(u + r_j) in v1 Equation 2 to x_i^j u + r_j in v2 Equation 1. This revises the mathematical description of the existing model. Neither version provides a substantial theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: v2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion elevate a new specific mechanism claim: TabPFN v2 internalizes attribute-token learning and infers attribute relationships during inference. v1 emphasized randomized tokens as a heterogeneity solution and claimed their applicability to other deep tabular models; that transfer contribution is removed. Feature-encoder and scalability claims remain.

C2.justification: v1's inverse-PCA explanation is replaced by interpretations of attention progressing from label-focused processing to inter-attribute relationships. v2 also explains unsupervised embedding weaknesses through delayed label supervision, motivates class permutations through artificial coding correlations, and identifies performance conditions through meta-features. It newly bounds its investigation to the released model because training data and recipes are unavailable.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents GPU/CPU hardware, links the group-size-one checkpoint used for Figure 3, supplies unsupervised-baseline code references, and specifies PCA dimensionality and additional variant implementation details in Appendices A–C. These extend reproducibility information without establishing that previously undisclosed hardware or settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including TabM, TabICL, MotherNet, fine-tuned in-context transformers, and s1. It also explicitly attributes decimal encoding to the already-cited TabDPT work, distinguishing its permutation extension. These update positioning within the same literature rather than replacing the paper's research context.

P1.justification: The introduction and mechanism discussion are extensively rewritten, contributions are reorganized into three principal insights, and section titles become more explanatory. Related-work material moves from v1 Appendix A into the main text, while the appendices are reorganized into separate evaluation, implementation, feature-extraction, analysis, and results sections.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Architecture and ranking diagrams are combined, three scalability charts are merged into Figure 5, and the original four-dataset embedding figure is split between main text and appendix with revised markers. New attention, embedding-comparison, and decision-tree displays accompany expanded tables; the randomized-token comparison displays are removed.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's indirect token-transfer tests, v2 provides direct attention probes, unsupervised embedding controls, a matched-budget DPT comparison, and better implementation disclosure. These strengthen evidential support and reproducibility. The gains are tempered by unexplained replacement of all 29 Vanilla embedding scores and a reporting inconsistency: v2 specifies ECOC for the main many-class evaluation, but Table 9 includes values matching the proposed extension rather than ECOC in Table 11. The net improvement is therefore limited.
